newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end with gains but volume drops.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end with gains but volume drops.

text.p: Greek shares managed to settle with light gains after a dull session but trading volume dropped to a thin 2.28 billion drachmas as a wave of strikes protesting Greece's austere 1995 budget hit the country.
Four AThens brokers were barred from trading in Thursday's session after failing to comply with a tight 48-hour settlement rule.
Market watchers expected a subdued market this week.

"The exchange is not tolerating settlement beyond T+2, thus eliminating short selling. The strict implementation of the T+2 deadline is particularly onerous on foreign investors who will inevitably cause local brokers to be barred from trading repetitively, until the new system is ironed out," said ING Barings.
Greece is cutting the marker 12-month T-bill rate by 50 basis points down to 11.50 percent in December.

Last Friday, Italy's Concretum agreed to buy a 12 percent stake in Heracles Cements for 32.23 billion drachmas or 5,320 drachmas a share from National Bank. Shares of Heracles closed unchanged at 3,050 drachmas on light volume.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.27 percent or 2.44 points higher at 910.52 from Wednesday's 908.08 close after opening at 907.52. Turnover was 2.28 billion drachmas after 30 on volume of 1.15 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 91 to 88 with 33 issues unchanged on 212 traded.
Banks were up 0.04 percent, industrials settled 0.46 percent firmer with construction slipping 0.23 percent. Small-caps closed down 0.28 percent.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted slightly higher at 547-565. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, gained 10 drachmas to close at 4,160.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $8.16-$9.16. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 2,874-3,056 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
